evidence: Receiving DO2 online trace: stable ~13 mg/L until t=46h, then step crash to 5.85 (46.2h), 4.58 (48h), 3.63 (51h), 3.27 mg/L (52h), still falling toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Assay clock: latest product assay is t=48h sample delivered at 52h (2.92 g/L); product concentration data too delayed to use for this DO emergency

Forward model (nominal, source-calibrated): keep 3.8h below limit min DO 1.53; increase_air 6.8h below; reduce_feed 6.4h below; combined 4.0h below; strong_feed_reduction 1.2h below, min DO 1.85, deficit 0.10 mg·h/L, product mass 189 kg (highest of all actions)
Model sensitivity: strong_feed_reduction is the only action with feasible sensitivity members and the highest mass range, while single-knob actions remain dominated by infeasible members
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 crashed from ~13 mg/L to 3.27 mg/L between 46-52h and is still falling; the trajectory breaches the 2.0 mg/L floor under KEEP. The nominal source-calibrated forward model indicates the receiving vessel has ~half the nominal oxygen transfer and that air increase alone or mild feed reduction leaves 6-7h of DO-limit violation. Strong feed reduction (0.6x) plus 15% air increase is the only bounded intervention that (a) cuts the metabolic oxygen demand driving the crash, (b) approaches the DO floor (predicted min 1.85, ~1.2h marginal exceedance vs 3.8-6.8h for alternatives), and (c) preserves and actually maximizes counted product mass (~189 kg vs 157 kg KEEP), avoiding a stop which yields zero production.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated approximation, not the hidden receiving realization; even the recommended action predicts a brief marginal DO excursion below 2.0 mg/L (deficit ~0.10 mg·h/L, sensitivity min-DO range 1.13-2.46), so residual infeasibility risk remains. The 4h assay delay means true product state is uncertain. If DO2 does not recover within ~4h of the intervention, escalation or batch termination review would be needed.
